correctness.rationale: All stationary entries follow from a positive Poisson-resolvent integral for unequal independent zero-temperature Lindblad loss rates. Exact T=diag(t,-t,v) and spin-flip X-state concurrence reduce the theorem to the explicitly derived sign polynomial for v-t and a balanced-envelope inequality 1-t²-v_bal²=4r(S³+S²r-r³)/[(S+r)²(S+2r)²]>0 for r≤S. This proves the unique universal CHSH threshold, equality case, high-reset invariance, and opposing strict product order over the full parameter domain. The standalone checker passed 6,895 symbolic/numerical assertions, including independently solved 16-dimensional Lindblad resolvents and spin-flip eigenvalue checks. Finite tests are not substituted for analytic proofs.

value.rationale: A natural experimentally relevant variable, the allocation of fixed total spontaneous-emission loss across two qubits, completely disappears from the optimized Bell test above one sharp rate while remaining strictly visible to concurrence. The proved witness-branch boundary and opposite strict monotonicities below that rate explain how two central quantum-correlation diagnostics can respond in opposite directions to physically unequal noise. This is an exact all-parameter identifiability and phase classification, not a textbook numerical evaluation or the known symmetric-limit formula.
